items.title: Invitation to the launch of MARSAD-Research Observatory on Socioeconomic Disparities in the Arab Mashreq
items.body:
Dear Students,

The Department of Economics at the Lebanese American University is pleased to invite you to the launch of
MARSAD , a data-driven research observatory focused on socioeconomic
 disparities in the Arab Mashreq. The launch event will take place on Friday, October 30, 2026, from 9:00 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. in AKSOB 903, LAU Beirut Campus,
and will also be streamed online via Webex .

The event will bring together distinguished scholars, researchers, and experts to discuss key socioeconomic challenges in the Arab Mashreq. The program will feature keynote
 addresses by internationally recognized economists Dr. Ragui Assaad, Professor and Freeman Chair for International Economic Policy at the University of Minnesota, and
Dr. Francisco Ferreira, Amartya Sen Professor of Inequality Studies at the London School of Economics, alongside three thematic panels focusing on
poverty, inequality, and economic development
in the Arab Mashreq.

We would be honored to have you join us for this important event.
Kindly confirm your attendance by completing this  form.

Please find the preliminary program agenda below:

- Agenda
 MARSAD \- Launch Event \- English version.pdf

- Agenda
 MARSAD \- Launch Event \- Arabic version.pdf

We look forward to your participation.

All the best,

Jamal Ibrahim Haidar

Assistant Professor of Economics, LAU

Chairperson, Department of Economics, LAU

items.title: Discover the New Minor in Pharmaceutical Engineering – Join Our Info Session!
items.place: LAU Byblos – Chagoury Health Sciences Auditorium - 📅
items.body:
Dear students,

Are you curious about how medicines are designed, formulated, and manufactured at scale?

The
School of Engineering and the School of Pharmacy are excited to invite you to an upcoming information session introducing the new
Minor in Pharmaceutical Engineering!

This joint initiative offers an interdisciplinary pathway combining engineering principles with pharmaceutical sciences to prepare you for high-impact careers in healthcare, biotechnology, and medicine manufacturing.

Event Details:

-
 📍 Location: LAU Byblos – Chagoury Health Sciences Auditorium

-
 📅 Date: Tuesday, November 3, 2026

-
 ⏰ Time: 3:00 PM

About the Minor

-
18 credits: two core courses, one from each school (CHE 200 and PHA 312), plus four electives of your choice
-
Open to Pharmacy and Chemical Engineering majors (students from other majors may request approval )
-
Builds skills in drug formulation, drug delivery systems, manufacturing and quality control
-
Opens doors to pharmaceutical and biotech companies, regulatory agencies and research institutions

At the session, we will walk you through the courses, when they are offered, how to fit the minor into your study plan, and how to declare it. Faculty from both schools will be
 there to answer your questions.

Read more about the minor here:

We look forward to seeing you there!

items.title: Deadline for Withdrawals (WP/WF) – Fall 2026
items.blurb: Last day to withdraw (WP/WF) from Fall 2026 courses — the deadline is midnight.
items.body:
A Kind Reminder

Dear Students,

The deadline to withdraw (WP/WF) from Fall 2026 courses is
November 09, midnight.

*The academic advisors at the Dean of Students office can help you identify the courses to withdraw from in order to maintain a good academic standing. You can get in touch with them by clicking on

this link.*

* *

You can submit a n
online Withdrawal (WP/WF) form for any of your Fall 2026 courses by following the process below:

1. Login using your LAU credentials to the
 Portal
 and navigate to “My Courses” > ”Registrar’s Office Forms”
2.
 Under “New Request” select “Forms” then ”Withdrawal Form (WP/WF)”

3.
 Fill in the required fields
4.
 Submit the form. The form will then be directed to your instructor who will take the appropriate action
5.
 You will receive an automatic notification once the Registrar’s Office process es the form
6.
 You can check your schedule through Banner to confirm that your withdrawal request was processed successfully.

Note:   If you have any difficulty submitting the online WP/WF form, please
 contact Ms. Lynn El-Radi:
lynn.el\-radi@lau.edu.lb
/ Ext. 1395
(Beirut Campus)
or Mr. Boulos Sakr: boulos.sakr@lau.edu.lb / Ext. 2846 (Byblos Campus).

*This is a no-reply email. For inquiries, please contact

items.title: Join LAU at the Spinneys Beirut Marathon 2026!
items.blurb: Run or volunteer with LAU — this year LAU runs for Liver Health. The first 100 to register for the 6K Fun Run are fully covered.
items.details: Registration booths: Oct 26 – Nov 5, Mon–Thu, 12:00–2:00 PM · Beirut: Upper Gate · Byblos: in front of Architecture Hall
items.body:
Dear Students,

We are pleased to invite you to join LAU at the upcoming Spinneys Beirut Marathon 2026, taking place on
Sunday, November 29, whether you would like to participate as a
runner or support the event as a
volunteer.

This year, LAU is proudly running for Liver Health.

Special Offer – Register Early!

LAU will fully cover the registration fees for the first 100 participants to register for the 6K Fun Fund Run! Don't miss this opportunity to be part of this exciting event at no cost.

Visit Our Campus Registration Booths:

- Beirut Campus: Upper Gate
- Byblos Campus: In front of Architecture Hall

Dates: October 26 – November 5 (Monday to Thursday)

Time: 12:00 PM – 2:00 PM

If you have any questions or need assistance with your registration, please visit our booths to inquire/register for:

- 6K Fund Run
- Competitive Races (10K, 21K, and 42K)
- Volunteers (Open to Students, Faculty, and Staff)

We will be available daily from Monday through Thursday, from 12:00 PM to 2:00 PM.

We look forward to seeing you represent LAU at the Beirut Marathon.

items.title: Library Monthly spotlight: LAU's Poster collection
items.body:
Dear LAU Community,

The LAU Libraries is home to some amazing resources! In our October spotlight, we will bring some of these resources straight to your inbox.

 This month's spotlight resource is....

What?  LAU's Poster collection

Who can benefit?  Anyone who is interested in graphic design, the history of theater at LAU, or is just looking for
 a bit of LAU nostalgia.

How to access?

-
 LAU:
 School of Arts & Sciences. Dept. of Communication Arts:\(Major Productions\) — 65 posters documenting major theatrical and musical productions.
-
 LAU.
 School of Arts & Sciences. Dept. of Communication Arts:(Student
 Productions\) — 314 posters showcasing the creativity and artistic achievements of LAU students.
-
 LAU
 Poster Collection \(donated by Rami Al Khal\) — 56 historical posters documenting activities associated with BUC, BCW, and LAU.

Hungry for more?  V isit the
LAU Libraries Archives & Special Collections  page
 to explore these collections and discover the stories preserved through these remarkable posters.
